newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga reopens taps on Vigdis oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Saga reopens taps on Vigdis oilfield.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Wednesday it had resumed oil production at the North Sea Vigdis oilfield following a series of shutdowns linked to a fault in the gas compressor system.
"We turned on the taps on Monday, but there was very little oil. Today we are producing 40,000 barrels," a Saga spokeswoman told Reuters.
The spokeswoman said output was expected to reach 70,000 barrels per day, but she was unable to say by when.
Vigdis was shut in on July 17 after a series of production stops since April.
The field was pumping around 40,000 bpd before the latest shutdown. Since it came on stream on January 28, five months ahead of schedule, it has pumped around three million barrels.
Due to restrictions on gas flaring by Norwegian authorities, crude production at Vigdis is dependent on the gas compressor system.
